lessons: Tonight's 17-land BG went 1-2 in games of 14 to 24 turns, contradicting the guide's 16-land rule; keep 16 unless the top end truly needs the extra land.
Stop taking second copies of unplayable tricks: my two Moonmists and two Vampiric Furies made no deck, and those picks should have gone to playable two-drops.
Count flier answers before building: Naturalize only hits enchantments and artifacts, so it was dead against round one's Chapel Geist and Voiceless Spirit, a 0-2 loss.
Take white removal and fliers early: Fiend Hunter, Smite the Monstrous and Bonds of Faith carried this WR deck to a 6-0 game record, with Chapel Geist and Voiceless Spirit closing games.
Expect long games: the WU matchup ran 24 and 28 turns, so evasive finishers like Midnight Haunting and Falkenrath Marauders mattered more than raw power against stalled boards.
Build a low curve on 17 lands (10 Plains, 7 Mountain), as the 3-0 deck did, and cut Butcher's Cleaver for cheaper creatures and removal.
Contrary to the guide's 16-land rule, my WU deck ran 17 lands on a 2-3 drop curve, and I lost a 47-turn round-three game to BG; play 16 lands with a low curve like the BG decks.
I took Spider Spawning second in pack one, then went WU and never played it; the guide says commit to a main colour by pick 5, and tonight's only 3-0 deck was WR, not BG.
My WU deck had five fliers yet still lost a 47-turn round-three game to BG's ground bodies, so fliers alone don't break stalls; pair them with removal and a faster clock.
Mono-red 17-Mountain aggro went 5-3 in games, but its games ran 15 to 29 turns, so early pressure didn't close; draft reach and card-advantage removal like Harvest Pyre before a third one-drop.
Blue never became splashable without fixing, so my notes ended mono-red; commit to a second colour's playables early instead of hoping for a late splash.
Round 1's WU deck with Claustrophobia, 2x Rebuke and Smite the Monstrous outlasted my red creatures; prefer threats that leave value when removed, like Pitchburn Devils, over plain bodies.
Tonight contradicted the guide: no BG deck went 3-0. BG seats finished 1-2, 2-1 and 2-1, and the 3-0 was WR seat 1. Treat BG as good, not proven.
The guide's 'keep Naturalize main against green fatties' is wrong because Naturalize cannot touch creatures. I ran two. Main creature removal such as Victim of Night or Corpse Lunge instead.
I lost 0-2 to WR's fliers-and-removal deck and took Wreath of Geists twice without playing it. Take removal or evasive threats over Wreath.

Count the pod's removal before pick 10: BG and UB drafters here ran two Naturalize, two Prey Upon, Victim of Night, and two Sensory Deprivation, so favor card advantage and evasion over one-for-one bodies.
With Bloodline Keeper's 2BB, Curse of Death's Hold, and Corpse Lunge in the deck, my 10 Plains/7 Swamp split was a real colour risk; go 9/8 or cut the double-black cards.
My games stalled to 20-32 turns without a clear finisher, so keep at least one reliable closer like Bloodline Keeper and avoid cutting too many cheap pressure creatures for marginal card quality.
Keep one flexible answer main: my BG deck had no Naturalize or Urgent Exorcism and lost 0-2 to a BG deck with two Naturalize, two Prey Upon and Night Terrors.
Where tonight contradicted the guide: my 17-land BG deck won 2-1 with Kindercatch and 5-drops, so 16 lands is not mandatory when the top end is heavy.
Don't take Falkenrath Marauders second pick in pack 2 when black is set; I cut all red and it never made the deck.
Liliana of the Veil needs BB, but I ran 5 Swamps to 11 Islands; count double-pip cards before setting the land split, not after.
Round 3's red aggro deck beat my slow blue-black control 2-1 in 23-29 turn games; prioritise two-drops and early evasive threats over a third cheap blocker.
Long stalled games against black-green (18-31 turns) show blue-black control needs real finishers; I had only Galvanic Juggernaut and Stitched Drake, so draft more threats than walls.
